item.title: [7.0] CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Recent advances in inference-time scaling have significantly improved the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs). However, these methods typically rely on repeated generation or external verification. To address this limitation, we introduce CritICL, a novel inference-time framework that improves reasoning while maintaining high efficiency.

WHY IT MATTERS

CritICL introduces a novel inference-time scaling approach that leverages small model failure modes to guide larger models efficiently, offering a practical alternative to compute-heavy verification methods.

item.title: [6.8] Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Zero-shot cross-task generalization, where a policy must execute manipulation tasks never seen during training, remains a central challenge in robot learning. In large language models, a novel task can be performed simply by specifying it in the context, without any parameter update. This form of in-context learning (ICL) turns generalization into a problem of task specification.

WHY IT MATTERS

Zero-WAM introduces a promising in-context learning paradigm using human video guidance for robotic manipulation, supported by a novel automated data generation pipeline (HumanGen).
